 Inside Apple TV’s explosive new schedule: Jamie Dornan’s high-stakes Zurich heist, Stephen Graham’s asylum terror, and Chris Pratt’s dramatic return
 Redazione 
 25 Ottobre 2026 
 / 4 min read 6 
 0 
 A heavyweight lineup of psychological thrillers and cinematic blockbusters is heading directly to the platform · Illustration: AI-generated image (Gemini) 
 In this story 
 Psychological terror and high-value heists take centre stage 
 Comebacks, culinary heritage, and trailblazing true stories 
 Groundbreaking cinema and family drama round out the roster 
 A formidable roster of prestige television, gripping crime sagas, and major studio features is heading to subscriber screens as the platform prepares its most ambitious season yet. Anchored by intense psychological suspense and globe-trotting action, the upcoming Apple TV releases place Hollywood heavyweights directly into calculated cat-and-mouse standoffs and deeply personal human journeys.
 The immediate priority for viewers seeking sharp narrative intrigue begins on the ground with high-stakes international crime before expanding into historical milestones and sharp sports satire.
 Psychological terror and high-value heists take centre stage
 Leading the dramatic charge is the psychological crime thriller Nocturne , adapted by Rowan Joffé and John Hlavin from the bestselling Lars Kepler novels. Liev Schreiber commands the screen as retired Philadelphia homicide detective Jonah Lynn, whose search for quietude in rural Pennsylvania is violently shattered by the machinations of an incarcerated serial killer named Jurek Walter, played by Stephen Graham .
 The suspense intensifies when a long-vanished victim suddenly reappears, compelling Lynn to send his surrogate daughter, FBI agent Saga Bauer, portrayed by Zazie Beetz , into the harrowing corridors of a maximum- security psychiatric institution. Featuring Bill Camp, Rory Culkin, and Chrissy Metz, the production rolls out new episodes weekly throughout the month following its initial two-episode launch.
 The adrenaline sharpens further with 12 12 12 , an eight-part European heist thriller from creators Jim Keeble and Dudi Appleton. The narrative pits a disgraced FBI agent, played by Anthony Mackie , against an elusive master criminal portrayed by Jamie Dornan , centered on an audacious raid against an impenetrable bank vault beneath Zurich.
 Three timelines, one fractured reality
 Directed in part by Kari Skogland, the production dispenses with traditional linear storytelling to engineer continuous suspense across three interconnected operational phases:
 The Twelve Months: Tracking the calculated surveillance, logistical preparations, and fragile criminal alliances assembled across Europe.
 The Twelve Hours: Capturing the suffocating real-time tension inside the subterranean Zurich vault during the breach.
 The Twelve Days: Documenting the chaotic international fallout, betrayals, and law enforcement dragnet that ensue.
 Co-starring Jack Kesy, Agathe Rousselle, and Kali Reis, the thriller presents a stylised, puzzle-box narrative designed to keep audiences dissecting every operational clue.
 Comebacks, culinary heritage, and trailblazing true stories
 Lightening the atmospheric tension without sacrificing narrative pace, the sports comedy Stick returns for its second season under creator Jason Keller. Owen Wilson reprises his role as former professional golfer Pryce Cahill, balancing his mentorship of teenage phenom Santi, played by Peter Dager, with an audacious bid to become the oldest player to ever win a major championship.
 The returning ensemble of Marc Maron, Mariana Treviño, Lilli Kay, Judy Greer, and Timothy Olyphant receives a notable boost as Rhea Seehorn steps onto the fairway as Cahill’s exacting new swing coach.

 Unscripted programming receives an equally personal narrative in Awkwafina: The Unlikely Cook . The eight-part documentary follows Nora Lum as she embarks on a cross-country culinary trial to master the heritage techniques needed to resurrect her family’s historic Cantonese restaurant in Flushing, New York.
 Training under celebrated culinary masters Roy Choi and Martin Yan, as well as faculty at the Culinary Institute of America , Lum travels alongside Jimmy O. Yang before putting her skills to the test in a high-pressure pop-up dinner staged for her grandmother and local community patrons.
 Groundbreaking cinema and family drama round out the roster
 Feature films occupy an equally prominent space in the scheduled Apple TV releases , led by the Academy Award-winning filmmaker Siân Heder’s biographical drama Being Heumann . Adapted from disability rights pioneer Judith Heumann ’s memoir, the film reconstructs the historic 1977 San Francisco sit-in that forced the enforcement of landmark civil protections.
 Ruth Madeley delivers a commanding performance as Heumann alongside Mark Ruffalo as federal official Joseph Califano, supported by Dylan O’Brien, Madeline Delp, and Rob Delaney. The production establishes a vital benchmark in screen authenticity, assembling the largest ensemble of disabled actors in a major studio dramatic release.
 Closing the schedule is the family adventure Way of the Warrior Kid , directed by McG and scripted by Will Staples from the bestselling novel by former Navy SEAL Jocko Willink. Chris Pratt stars as Jake, a wounded Navy SEAL who moves in with his sister, played by Linda Cardellini, and her son Marc, portrayed by Jude Hill.
 Facing aggressive school bullying, young Marc undergoes a transformative summer training regimen focused on swimming, physical stamina, and mental fortitude to reclaim his self-belief. Meanwhile, live sports fans can immediately track the intense rivalry unfolding in Major League Soccer, as Los Angeles FC squares off against the LA Galaxy on the platform’s live schedule.
 💡 With heavy-hitting thrillers and historic dramatic productions arriving side by side, subscribers face a remarkably packed viewing calendar.
 🔍 From the psychological labyrinths of European banking vaults to the gritty personal grit of civil rights history, these ambitious titles highlight a strategic push towards top-tier cinematic storytelling.
